answer: Submissions that land within 155 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The crystal detector writes to dune, and sable publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 121 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 16 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
